# OrchestrAI V2 (Control Plane) submission

`test-playbooks-orchestrai.yml` with `use_v2=true` runs exactly like the default
path: Detect & Trigger, one `Test <playbook> (<os>/<device>)` job per playbook and
configuration, then Test Gate. Only the submission changes. Detect & Trigger
starts each batch through the Control Plane CI API (GitHub OIDC, no stored
OrchestrAI token) instead of Jenkins, waits until the Control Plane has started
that batch's Jenkins build, and hands the build URL to the per-playbook jobs.
Those jobs read the build's `summary.json` as before.

The tested source is `amd/playbooks` at `playbook_ref`, resolved to a commit SHA.

## ReportPortal

On by default (`v2_publish_reportportal`) until V2 reporting replaces it. The
Control Plane publishes with the workspace credential named by
`ORCHESTRAI_V2_RP_CREDENTIAL` to `ORCHESTRAI_V2_RP_PROJECT`, and the publish is
required. Each per-playbook summary links the launch the publisher logs.

## Configuration

Repository variables: `ORCHESTRAI_V2_CI_API_URL`, `ORCHESTRAI_V2_OIDC_AUDIENCE`,
`ORCHESTRAI_V2_PORTAL_URL`, `ORCHESTRAI_V2_WORKSPACE` (the workspace slug), and
optionally `ORCHESTRAI_V2_LINUX_IMAGE` / `ORCHESTRAI_V2_WINDOWS_IMAGE`. The
existing driver, hardware-tag, ROCm index, TheRock and `ORCHESTRAI_PIPELINE_*`
settings are reused; the per-playbook jobs still read the Jenkins build.

The workspace CI access rule must trust `amd/playbooks`, the ref, the event, and
the workflow `amd/playbooks/.github/workflows/test-playbooks-orchestrai.yml@<ref>`.

Cancelling the GitHub run does not cancel started V2 runs; the Control Plane
run timeout bounds them, as Jenkins builds were bounded before.
